answer_core:
I would not choose the Silva direction yet, but I also would not retreat automatically to the safer lab path. The decision should turn on executability, not on which story feels more exciting or safer.

Run a short Silva reality check only if it can answer concrete questions: can you access usable data soon, get enough collaborator depth to offset the lab's single-cell gap, and secure explicit advisor support? A hot field plus uncertain data is not yet a dissertation plan.

At the same time, protect the fallback before you rely on it. The fallback is real only if it remains advisor-backed, funded, technically ready, identity-coherent, and available at the trigger date. An 18-month pivot is not safe if the thing you pivot back to quietly disappears.

Sequence matters: advisor first, low-cost Silva evidence second, committee only after the data path is real. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal, do not run all options in parallel, and do not use broad PhD success-rate claims as probabilities for your case.
